plants.name: Hoya carnosa 'Krimson Queen'
plants.tip: The variegation sits on the leaf edge, so it scorches in hard sun. Bright indirect light holds the pink.
plants.colour: Mid-green centre with cream and pink outer margins

plants.name: Hoya carnosa 'Krimson Princess'
plants.tip: The pale centre carries little chlorophyll, so growth is slow. Do not try to push it with extra feed.
plants.colour: Cream to pink centre with a green margin, new stems flushed red

plants.name: Hoya carnosa 'Compacta' (Hindu rope)
plants.tip: Water sits in the twisted leaves and rots them. Water at the pot rim and let the compost dry right out.
plants.colour: Tightly curled, crowded green leaves, often edged cream

plants.name: Hoya carnosa 'Krinkle 8'
plants.tip: Slow to fill a pot. Leave it slightly rootbound rather than moving it up a size each spring.
plants.colour: Green leaves dimpled with about eight sunken puckers each

plants.name: Hoya carnosa 'Chelsea'
plants.tip: The thick cupped leaves store water, so it forgives a missed fortnight far better than a soggy pot.
plants.colour: Thick, cupped, deep green leaves with sunken veins

plants.name: Hoya carnosa 'Grey Ghost'
plants.tip: The silver flecking thins out in low light. A metre from an east window keeps new leaves dense.
plants.colour: Green leaves almost covered in dense silver flecking

plants.name: Hoya carnosa 'Freckles'
plants.tip: Speckling is strongest on leaves grown in bright light. Older leaves from a dim spell stay plain.
plants.colour: Deep green with scattered silver speckles

plants.name: Hoya carnosa 'Wilbur Graves'
plants.tip: A vigorous climber. Give it a trellis early, because the stems set their direction once they go woody.
plants.colour: Large green leaves heavily splashed with silver

plants.name: Hoya pubicalyx 'Splash'
plants.tip: One of the readiest hoyas to flower indoors. A few hours of direct morning sun brings the buds on.
plants.colour: Narrow dark green leaves flecked with silver

plants.name: Hoya pubicalyx 'Royal Hawaiian Purple'
plants.tip: Flower colour deepens in strong light. Never cut off the bare flower spur, as the next buds form on it.
plants.colour: Dark green leaves, deep wine-red flowers with a near-black sheen

plants.name: Hoya pubicalyx 'Red Buttons'
plants.tip: Leave the old flower stalks in place. It reblooms from the same short spur for years.
plants.colour: Green leaves with light silver flecks, small dark red flowers

plants.name: Hoya kerrii (sweetheart hoya)
plants.tip: A single rooted leaf almost never grows on. Buy a cutting with a length of stem if you want a vine.
plants.colour: Thick, plain green heart-shaped leaves

plants.name: Hoya kerrii 'Variegata'
plants.tip: Very slow, and rot follows overwatering quickly. Wait until the leaves feel slightly soft before watering.
plants.colour: Heart-shaped leaves, green centre with a broad butter-yellow margin

plants.name: Hoya kerrii 'Splash'
plants.tip: It sits still for a year or two, then runs. Keep the pot small and the compost gritty and open.
plants.colour: Heart-shaped green leaves with fine silver flecking

plants.name: Hoya obovata
plants.tip: The round leaves hold weeks of water between them. Overwatering, not neglect, is what kills it.
plants.colour: Round, thick, deep green leaves flecked with silver

plants.name: Hoya diversifolia
plants.tip: A large grower that flowers freely once mature. Give it a support and room to climb properly.
plants.colour: Broad, flat, leathery grey-green leaves

plants.name: Hoya australis
plants.tip: Takes more direct sun than most hoyas, and it needs that sun before it will flower.
plants.colour: Glossy round mid-green leaves, thick and waxy

plants.name: Hoya australis 'Lisa'
plants.tip: The cream centre burns in midday sun. Bright light through a curtain keeps the colour without scorch.
plants.colour: Green leaves with a yellow-cream centre, pink on new growth

plants.name: Hoya bella
plants.tip: The thin leaves dry out far faster than a carnosa. Water weekly and keep it out of a draught.
plants.colour: Small pointed mid-green leaves on fine trailing stems

plants.name: Hoya linearis
plants.tip: The one hoya that hates heat and dry air. Keep it cool, humid and evenly moist or it drops whole strands.
plants.colour: Soft, downy, needle-thin pale green leaves hanging in curtains

plants.name: Hoya lacunosa
plants.tip: The small white flowers are strongly scented in the evening. Site it where that is welcome at night.
plants.colour: Small dark green diamond-shaped leaves with sunken veins

plants.name: Hoya lacunosa 'Eskimo'
plants.tip: Prefers steady moisture to the hard dry-out a carnosa wants. Never let the leaves shrivel.
plants.colour: Dark green leaves dusted with pale silver flecking

plants.name: Hoya curtisii
plants.tip: It creeps flat rather than climbing. A wide shallow pot fills in far faster than a deep one.
plants.colour: Tiny spade-shaped leaves, olive green with silver marbling

plants.name: Hoya wayetii
plants.tip: The dark leaf margin only develops in good light. In shade the new leaves come through plain green.
plants.colour: Long narrow leaves, deep green with a chocolate-brown margin

plants.name: Hoya krohniana
plants.tip: Small leaves mean a small water reserve. Check it weekly rather than on a fortnightly routine.
plants.colour: Small heart-shaped leaves, dark green with silver flecks

plants.name: Hoya macrophylla 'Albomarginata'
plants.tip: The large leaves guttate and drip sticky sap. Stand it where a marked floor will not matter.
plants.colour: Large ribbed leaves, green with a broad cream border

plants.name: Hoya multiflora (shooting star)
plants.tip: It grows as an upright shrub, not a vine, and flowers repeatedly through the year in good light.
plants.colour: Long glossy green leaves, swept-back white and yellow flowers

plants.name: Hoya retusa
plants.tip: The needle leaves scorch in direct sun and rot in wet compost. Bright shade and a fast, gritty mix.
plants.colour: Flat, grass-like green leaves in dense tufts

plants.name: Hoya serpens
plants.tip: A cool-growing species that sulks in a warm room. Keep it humid and away from radiators.
plants.colour: Small round fuzzy leaves, pale green with faint flecks

plants.name: Hoya polyneura (fishtail hoya)
plants.tip: Thin leaves and shallow roots. It wants humidity and even moisture, never a complete dry-out.
plants.colour: Thin green leaves with pale veining, shaped like a fishtail

plants.name: Hoya cumingiana
plants.tip: It stands upright rather than trailing, and flowers readily on young plants in bright light.
plants.colour: Small stiff dark green leaves in neat pairs up upright stems

plants.name: Hoya shepherdii
plants.tip: The roots resent disturbance. Repot only when the compost has broken down, not on a schedule.
plants.colour: Long, narrow, downward-hanging green leaves

plants.name: Hoya 'Mathilde'
plants.tip: A carnosa and serpens cross that flowers young. Bright light and a full dry-out between waterings.
plants.colour: Small round semi-succulent leaves flecked with silver

plants.name: Hoya 'Rebecca'
plants.tip: Flowers young and often. Leave the spur intact after the blooms drop and it will use it again.
plants.colour: Green leaves, lavender-pink flowers with a yellow centre

plants.name: Hoya 'Sunrise'
plants.tip: The red colouring is a response to strong light. In a shaded spot the leaves simply stay green.
plants.colour: Green leaves that flush deep red-bronze in strong light

plants.name: Hoya burtoniae
plants.tip: The leaf edges redden under bright light. Fast-growing, and easy to root from a two-node cutting.
plants.colour: Small fuzzy olive leaves with red edges in bright light

plants.name: Hoya caudata
plants.tip: Wants warmth and humidity. It stalls in a cold room and drops leaves in dry winter air.
plants.colour: Large mottled leaves, dark green splashed heavily with silver

plants.name: Hoya callistophylla
plants.tip: The vein pattern darkens as each leaf matures. Give it warmth, humidity and a pole to climb.
plants.colour: Long leaves with dark olive veins netted over pale green

plants.name: Hoya finlaysonii
plants.tip: A humidity lover with brittle leaves. Handle the stems rather than the leaves when training it.
plants.colour: Thick leaves with a dark sunken vein network over green

plants.name: Hoya nummularioides
plants.tip: Flowers heavily and young, with a strong evening scent. Keep it bright and slightly pot-bound.
plants.colour: Small round fuzzy green leaves in close pairs
